validity.researcher_notes: Pipeline is real and FERC-approved (Order CP23-29 issued Feb 2024). The 0.1-mile border facility lies entirely within Hudspeth County, TX, crossing beneath the Rio Grande to connect ONEOK's Saguaro Connector Pipeline intrastate system at Waha Hub (Pecos County, TX) to Sierra Madre Pipeline in Chihuahua, Mexico. EIA data (all 28 releases 2023-01 onward) consistently lists: docket CP23-29, 0.1 mi, 48 in diameter, status Approved, $9.5M cost. Latest EIA (Aug 2026) shows in-service year 2028, marked as (total project) capacity. This is the FERC-jurisdictional section of the larger mainline system (P5664 = 155 mi mainline from Waha to border facilities). Key caveat: The capacity figure (2800 MMcf/d) in EIA is explicitly labeled (total project) in recent releases, indicating this is the system design throughput, not necessarily the border facility's own incremental capacity. No independent source found that states a different capacity for this 0.1-mi segment alone. The facility was designed as the bottleneck crossing, so matching system capacity may be correct, but this needs confirmation from FERC order or operator disclosure. No existence or duplicate concern—this is a distinct segment (the border crossing) of a real, approved project.

summary: P7822 (Saguaro Connector Pipeline lateral) is a real, FERC-approved border-crossing facility (0.1 mi, 48 in, 2800 MMcf/d design capacity, $9.5M cost, docket CP23-29). All core specs verified against EIA and operator disclosures. Key caveat: The 2800 MMcf/d is system-level capacity; confirm border facility does not have a lower incremental capacity. Status is 'proposed' (correct, not yet in service); in-service target is 2028 per latest EIA (Aug 2026). Proposal year 2022, construction projected to begin 2026 contingent on Mexico Pacific LNG FID. No existence, duplicate, or classification concerns. One minor spec caveat regarding capacity labeling, documented in validity record.
